'''ǁXegwi''' or '''ǁXʼegwi''' (pronounced {{IPAc-en|ˈ|z|ɛ|g|w|i:}} {{respell|ZEH|gwee}}; {{langx|xeg|giǁkxi꞉gwi|links=no}}), also known as ''Batwa,'' is an extinct [[Tuu languages|ǃKwi language]] spoken at [[Lake Chrissie]] in [[South Africa]], near the [[Eswatini|Swazi]] border. The last known speaker, Jopi Mabinda (also Jobi Mabinda<ref name=":2" />), was murdered in 1988.<ref>{{cite book |last=Traill |first=A. |chapter=The Khoesan languages |editor-last=Mesthrie |editor-first=Rajend |title=Language in South Africa |publisher=Cambridge University Press |year=2002 |doi=10.1017/CBO9780511486692.003 |page=42|isbn=978-0-521-79105-2 }}</ref> However, a reporter for the South African newspaper ''[[Mail & Guardian]]'' reports that ǁXʼegwi may still be spoken in the [[Chrissiesmeer]] district.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Davie |first=Kevin |title=The secret pool of surviving Bushmen at Chrissiesmeer |url=http://mg.co.za/article/2011-06-24-the-secret-pool-of-surviving-bushmen-at-chrissiesmeer |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110729174225/http://mg.co.za:80/article/2011-06-24-the-secret-pool-of-surviving-bushmen-at-chrissiesmeer |archive-date=2011-07-29 |access-date=2018-03-04 |newspaper=The Mail & Guardian |language=en}}</ref>

The ǁXʼegwi name for their language has been spelled ''giǁkwi꞉gwi'' or ''kiǁkwi꞉gwi.''  Their name for themselves, {{Lang|xeg|Tlouʼeʼthle}} 'people of rock and water',<ref name=":0" /> has been transcribed ''tlou tle'' and ''kxlou-kxle'', presumably renderings of {{IPA|[k͡𝼄ouk͡𝼄e]}}.  The Nguni (Zulu and Swazi) called them ''(a)batwa'', ''amaNkqeshe'' and ''amaNgqwigqwi''; the Sotho called them ''Baroa''~''Barwa''.<ref>{{cite book |first=Yvonne |last=Treis |chapter=Names of Khoisan languages and their variants |title=Language, identity, and conceptualization among the Khoisan |editor-first=Mathias |editor-last=Schladt |publisher=Rüdiger Köppe Verlag |pages=463–503 |year=1998 |isbn=978-3-89645-143-9}}</ref>

==Phonology==

===Tone===
From Köhler's material, it appears that ǁXʼegwi had a four-tone inventory. 

===Consonants===
ǁXʼegwi lost the abrupt clicks (the various manners of [[palatal click|ǂ]] and [[alveolar click|ǃ]]) found in its relatives. It reacquired {{IPA|ǃ}} from [[Nguni languages|Nguni]] [[Bantu languages]], but clicks remained relatively infrequent, compared to other Tuu languages. It also had a series of [[uvular consonant|uvular]] [[plosives]] not found in other Tuu languages.<ref>{{cite AV media |first=Anthony |last=Traill |year=1999 |title=Extinct: South African Khoisan Languages |type=CD}}</ref>

Labialized consonants are recorded, both pulmonic and lingual; Honken (2020) interprets [CʷV] as /CoV/.

=== Word order ===
ǁXʼegwi exhibits [[Subject–verb–object word order|subject–verb–object]] (SVO) word order, as can be seen in the following examples:<ref name=":2">{{Cite book |last=Potgieter |first=E. F. |title=The disappearing Bushmen of Lake Chrissie - a preliminary survey |date=1955 |publisher=J. L. van Schaik |edition=With notes on the language by Dirk Ziervogel |series=Hidding-Currie publ. of the University of South Africa |volume=1 |location=Pretoria, South Africa}}</ref><!-- No interlinear in source -->
